notes.title: [Infection] Strange Sounds, Spreading Glitches
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/958fd0ac00775a54d26982ddb36da0e69aa0dda6.jpg[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

Lately, I’ve been noticing strange sounds.
Sometimes while I’m typing, my hearing seems to fade…
The familiar rhythm of keystrokes starts to blur together with a dry clattering noise.
Maybe it’s because I recently rewatched the trailer for DO NOT PLAY.
It sounded eerily similar to the faint rattling when that final character’s head begins to twitch at the end.

This month, glitches kept happening on my machine.
But it seems the same thing has begun appearing for other employees as well.
Just the other day, several members of the dev team told me their PCs were experiencing the same errors.
When I checked, it turned out to be the same kind of blue screens and corrupted text that I’d seen on my own terminal.
The corrupted text wasn’t identical, but… strangely close.

Could it be that the restored data itself carries bugs?
After all, we’ve all been sharing the recovered files within the team.
What if one of them is spreading—like some kind of virus?
For now, we’re replacing our machines to protect regular work,
but we’ll still need to analyze which of the restored files has been corrupted.

Employee A

notes.title: [Ominous] The Meeting Screen Looked Wrong—But Only for Me
notes.content:
It’s me. Employee A.

Lately, there’s been something strange happening during our online meetings.
Every now and then, the person on the other side of the camera looks… like someone else entirely.
Their voice, too—just slightly—sounds mechanical.
I kept telling myself it was nothing.
But during one meeting the other day, I knew for sure it wasn’t.

My screen was the only one acting up.
The video was distorted, and I couldn’t recognize a single face.
The emoji button I always use was warped, and the text looked like it had glitched into gibberish.
I grabbed my phone and snapped a picture in a hurry.

When I asked later, it turned out no one else had seen anything strange.
And yet… there was something even more unsettling.
Despite all the glitches, the red button that should have said “End Call” now just read “Call” —
as if it wasn’t meant to end anything, but to summon something.
It said only one word:

“call.”

It should have ended the meeting—but somehow, it felt like it was trying to summon something instead.
So I sat there, not touching it, until everyone else had left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/ded15bdb656520593d422fa964031592eb49cd8e.jpg[/img]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/370f264daf9852b26a4d066719951999b78d89d2.jpg[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

I had a strange dream recently.

There was a large box with holes shaped like triangles and diamonds on its lid.
It was a simple game—drop blocks of various shapes into the corresponding holes.
A triangle block fits through the triangle hole, a diamond block through the diamond hole...

But then it got more complicated.
Some blocks were combinations of two shapes, or long pieces that had to be joined together.
At the end, I didn’t have a round block, so I brought my right hand closer to my face.
The room went completely dark after that, so I never found out if I had finished.

notes.title: [Restart] Requesting Support from Another Team for the New Structure
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/6c276d99a7ec8cf8c77686e8a5d9082f186015e6.png[/img]

It’s me. Employee A.

There was a moment when I copied an entire folder—but when I checked, it was completely empty.
The folder had definitely been created, but there was nothing inside.
I tried copying it again, and this time, one of the files in the original folder had its name changed.
Its contents had been rewritten.
By who? When? How?
I can’t shake the feeling that someone is remotely accessing my machine—without permission.

Anyway, on to the main topic.
We can’t let the project stall just because the person in charge is still absent.
So, I reached out to another team to ask for someone who could take over the restoration work.
That said, people in the office are increasingly reluctant to talk about the project.
The atmosphere isn’t great.

“I heard they’re trying to gather new members for that project again.”
“One of the new members said they had a weird dream.”

Comments like that have started to pop up—around the sink, in the hallways.
Even so, we have to move forward.
Under a new structure, we’ll continue the restoration work as planned.

Employee A

notes.title: [Report] The Team Member Who Stopped Coming to Meetings Has Gone Missing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/d7f726bec937734f6eb03147f7cfad32bef3ac71.jpg[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

When I speak, it doesn’t sound like my own voice.
Even when I record and play it back, it’s definitely mine—but something feels off.
I talk every day, and yet, there’s a strange sense of disconnect.
It feels like someone else is speaking in my place.
I’m starting to forget what my own voice is supposed to sound like.

Also—
The team member who stopped coming to meetings due to health issues has now gone missing.
The last time he appeared was in an online meeting a few days ago.
We were relieved to see him finally show up, but his camera was off, and we couldn’t see his face.
I asked, “What happened with that screen?”
He typed a single message into the chat box in the meeting window:
“Forget about that.”
And then he left the call.

Worried, I sent him a personal message on LINE later that day.
He never read it.
We’d worked together on several projects, and I was genuinely concerned.
I even contacted his landlord, who told me he had moved out some time ago.

He’s vanished—there’s no other way to put it.
And now I keep wondering:
Was it really him on the other side of the screen that day?

The photo I took of him during the early days of the restoration—just his back, quietly working—
I may never see that again.
And the thought of that... is hard to accept.

notes.title: [Log] A Work Scene Filled with Someone’s Thoughts
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/5be1953553c5f17871169bd5421de74a3398c406.png[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

I thought I had been asleep… but when I came to, I was sitting in front of my computer.
On the screen was a block of unfamiliar text—something I don't remember typing.
The words “3:44 AM” were repeated over and over.
What was I doing, sneaking out of bed in the middle of the night...?

That reminded me—I once filmed the team member who stopped coming to meetings during the early days of development.
As the workday was winding down, I was doing my usual rounds of the office and found him still at his desk.
He was silently focused, breaking apart the inner workings of an old game, piece by piece—like solving a puzzle.
He told me he was carefully dismantling and reconstructing it, trying to understand how everything fit together.

At one point, he muttered to himself,
“Why did they write this part like this, I wonder…”
Then he gave a quiet laugh and said,
“But somehow… I kind of get it.”

In that moment, I realized he wasn’t just “restoring” the game.
He was trying to truly understand it—to connect with the thoughts of whoever created it, and the atmosphere of the time it was made.

notes.title: [Update] A Familiar Screen Has Reappeared
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/254bd2cbf6b22a9522c86fa7584345ae5b403706.png[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

The other day, when I returned to my desk, the screen had gone completely black.
It felt too soon for sleep mode, and when I tried to force a shutdown… suddenly, icons started appearing.
One of them looked like a face—something I’d never seen before.
I tried to take a picture, but it vanished before I could.
Even now, I can’t shake the feeling that something’s still watching me from the corner of the display.

Anyway, I found an old executable left on one of the floppy disks.
When I launched it, a familiar blue dolphin started bouncing around the screen.
It reminded me of elementary school—how I used to run it just to watch, without really knowing what it was for.
I think it was supposed to help with support or system navigation… maybe.
I can’t remember if it had anything to do with this game.
But there’s something oddly charming about the way it moves—though now, it almost feels like… it’s watching me, too.

notes.title: [Absent] A Team Member Who Stopped Coming to Meetings
notes.content:
It’s me. Employee A.

I felt like someone was standing just outside the door.
There was no sound—but I could feel someone there.
I checked the peephole. No one was there.
But when I came back, the coffee on my desk was noticeably lower.
I’m supposed to be alone in this room...

Also, one of the developers helping with the data restoration
has been missing some meetings, citing health issues.
With the recent extreme temperature swings, that’s understandable.

But… was he really unwell?
During a previous meeting, he’d seemed unusually excited, saying,
“I found something strange in the data.”
I’d asked him to show me what he meant—but never got a reply.

His last login time just remains there, never updating.
When I look at it, it feels as if someone—or something—has stopped his time alone.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/a4c0181e56dfb9fc78424bb1070efb32ba1953b2.jpg[/img]
It’s me. Employee A.

Lately, I’ve been feeling a strange weight on my shoulders.
At first, I thought it was just the weather, but something feels… off.
Ever since I started recovering data from the floppy disk, it’s like something’s been lingering just behind me.
I keep thinking I see movement out of the corner of my eye, but when I turn around, no one’s there.
And it’s been happening more and more often.

Just the other day, while I was going through the floppy with one of our developers,
we found something—something that caught our attention.

It looked like an image file, so I tried to open it.
The moment I did, the screen froze completely.
I couldn’t do anything. Everything just stopped.

This is the screen that got stuck.

What is this...?

notes.title: [Greeting] What Began on That Day
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45581669/286509c62fcde2ce0dfecf0c0df416f923dbb82b.jpg[/img]
It happened a long, long time ago.

A single URL, quietly posted in a forgotten corner of the internet.

“There’s a game you’re not supposed to play.”

That’s what someone said. Just a rumor, I thought. So casually, I clicked the link. That was the beginning.

I don’t remember much of the content. But I do remember the eerie atmosphere of the screen, the unsettling title, and a pop-up message that felt like a warning:
“Will you take the risk and play?”

Everything about it felt... off. Unnatural. Unreal.
And then—one of my friends, the one I talked to about the game, suddenly disappeared.
No one could reach them. Eventually, we just stopped hearing anything at all.
That stayed with me, buried deep in the back of my mind.

Years passed.
Eventually, I started asking around on social media, piecing together fragments from the depths of memory.
Maybe it was just a dream. Maybe it never existed.
But the certainty that I saw it that day… never left me.

After a string of coincidences, and with the help of many people, I finally found it.
The screen—just as it was.
The data—untouched, unchanged.

Even now, part of me still doesn’t want to believe it’s real.

But I’ve made up my mind. I’m going to bring it back—deliver it, with my own hands, to all of you.

To restore and rebuild the lost game—
And revive it under the name “DO NOT PLAY.”

Even now, as this game—once only a rumor—starts to become real, I can hardly believe it myself.

But there’s no turning back.

This is a journey through memory and the past—
And above all, a process of facing our fears.

The “DO NOT PLAY” Restoration Project begins now.

Please, come with me to the end of this story.

And don’t forget to add it to your wishlist.

– Employee A, SCRAP
